findings.title: Overweight
findings.clinicalExplanation: Current body weight is above the recommended healthy BMI range.
findings.userExplanation: Your current weight is above the healthy range for your height. Gradual improvements in nutrition, movement, and recovery may help improve overall health.
findings.clinicalImpact: Higher long-term risk of metabolic complications if associated with unhealthy lifestyle behaviours.

findings.title: Obesity
findings.clinicalExplanation: Current body weight falls into the obesity classification.
findings.userExplanation: Your current weight is significantly above the healthy range for your height. Focusing on sustainable lifestyle changes can have a major positive impact on your health.
findings.clinicalImpact: Increased risk for metabolic and cardiovascular conditions.

findings.title: Underweight
findings.clinicalExplanation: Current body weight is below the recommended healthy BMI range.
findings.userExplanation: Your current weight is below the healthy range. Focusing on balanced nutrition and healthy weight gain can support your overall energy and strength.
findings.clinicalImpact: Potential risk of nutrient deficiencies and lower immune function.

findings.title: Excess Body Fat
findings.clinicalExplanation: Estimated body fat is above the healthy range.
findings.userExplanation: Estimated body fat is above the healthy range. Improving body composition—not simply reducing body weight—should be a primary focus.

findings.title: Positive Energy Balance Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Several daily habits suggest overall energy intake regularly exceeds energy expenditure.
findings.userExplanation: Several daily habits suggest your overall energy intake may regularly exceed your energy expenditure. Rather than one single behaviour, it is the combination of these habits that is likely contributing to weight gain.

findings.title: Low Protein Intake
findings.clinicalExplanation: Dietary pattern indicates suboptimal protein intake for weight management.
findings.userExplanation: Your eating pattern may not consistently provide enough protein to support healthy weight management.
findings.clinicalImpact: May result in lower satiety and muscle loss during calorie deficit.

findings.title: High Sugar Intake
findings.clinicalExplanation: Responses suggest frequent intake of added sugars.
findings.userExplanation: Your responses suggest frequent intake of added sugars that may contribute to excess energy intake.
findings.clinicalImpact: Contributes to positive energy balance and blood sugar spikes.

findings.title: Irregular Eating Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Meal timing appears inconsistent throughout the day.
findings.userExplanation: Your meal timing appears inconsistent. Creating a more regular eating routine may improve hunger control and make healthy choices easier.
findings.clinicalImpact: Can disrupt hunger hormones and lead to overeating.

findings.title: Sedentary Lifestyle Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Prolonged sitting combined with limited movement and exercise.
findings.userExplanation: Your activity pattern suggests prolonged sitting combined with limited movement and exercise. Increasing daily movement may provide meaningful health benefits even before significant weight loss occurs.
findings.clinicalImpact: Lower daily energy expenditure and higher cardiometabolic risk.

findings.title: Recovery Deficit Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Recovery habits (sleep/stress) are not supporting metabolic health.
findings.userExplanation: Your recovery may not be fully supporting your health goals. Improving sleep quality and managing stress could make healthy eating and regular activity easier to maintain.
findings.clinicalImpact: Higher cortisol and dysregulated appetite hormones.

findings.title: High Stress Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Stress is affecting lifestyle habits and consistency.
findings.userExplanation: Stress may be affecting both your lifestyle habits and consistency.
findings.clinicalImpact: Can lead to emotional eating and poor sleep.

findings.title: Emotional Eating Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Eating behaviours appear influenced by emotional triggers rather than physical hunger.
findings.userExplanation: Your responses suggest that emotions and stress may sometimes influence your eating decisions. Addressing these triggers may help improve long-term consistency.
findings.clinicalImpact: Major barrier to sustaining a caloric deficit.

findings.title: Weight Cycling Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: History suggests repeated cycles of losing and regaining weight.
findings.userExplanation: Your history suggests repeated attempts to change weight. Focusing on sustainable habits rather than rapid results may improve long-term success.

findings.title: Unrealistic Expectations
findings.clinicalExplanation: Desired timeline does not align with a gradual, sustainable lifestyle approach.
findings.userExplanation: Your desired timeline may not align with a gradual, sustainable lifestyle approach.
findings.clinicalImpact: High risk of abandonment due to unmet expectations.

findings.title: Low Behaviour Readiness
findings.clinicalExplanation: User lacks confidence or support to make major changes currently.
findings.userExplanation: You may benefit from smaller, more achievable habit changes before pursuing larger goals.
findings.clinicalImpact: Requires adjusted coaching approach to build self-efficacy.

findings.title: Active Healthy Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Maintains high daily movement and structured exercise.
findings.userExplanation: You maintain a good level of daily physical activity, giving you a strong foundation.

findings.title: Balanced Nutrition Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Practices portion control, low sugar intake, and regular meals.
findings.userExplanation: Your eating habits already include several positive behaviours.

findings.title: Strong Recovery Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Reports good sleep, low stress, and good energy.
findings.userExplanation: Your recovery habits appear to be a strength, supporting your long-term health.
findings.clinicalImpact: Hormonal balance and better appetite regulation.

findings.title: High Readiness
findings.clinicalExplanation: High confidence and support.
findings.userExplanation: You have a strong mindset and support system to achieve your goals.
findings.clinicalImpact: Higher likelihood of long term success.

findings.title: Positive Energy Balance
findings.clinicalExplanation: Daily caloric intake exceeds total daily energy expenditure.
findings.userExplanation: Your daily habits suggest you are consistently taking in more energy than your body uses, which is the primary driver of weight gain.

findings.title: Recent Weight Loss
findings.clinicalExplanation: Patient reports recent intentional or unintentional weight loss.
findings.userExplanation: You've recently lost weight, which means your body may be in a state of metabolic adaptation. Maintaining this loss requires a sustainable approach.

findings.title: Weight Cycling
findings.clinicalExplanation: History of losing and regaining weight repeatedly.
findings.userExplanation: You have a history of weight cycling. This can make future weight loss harder due to metabolic adaptation, so a slow, consistent approach is essential.

findings.title: Repeated Diet Attempts
findings.clinicalExplanation: Multiple previous attempts at weight loss, indicating potential diet fatigue.
findings.userExplanation: You've tried several diets in the past. This time, focusing on adding healthy habits rather than just restricting food will help prevent burnout.

findings.title: Chronic Diet Cycling
findings.clinicalExplanation: Prolonged history of chronic dieting, highly predictive of metabolic resistance.
findings.userExplanation: Chronic dieting can slow your metabolism. We need to focus on nourishing your body properly rather than severe restriction.

findings.title: Low Meal Frequency
findings.clinicalExplanation: Eating very few times a day, which may lead to extreme hunger and overeating later.
findings.userExplanation: Eating infrequently can cause severe hunger, making it difficult to control portion sizes when you do eat.

findings.title: Frequent Eating
findings.clinicalExplanation: Eating multiple times a day, increasing the opportunity for caloric surplus.
findings.userExplanation: Eating frequently gives you more opportunities to over-consume calories, especially if snacks aren't planned.

findings.title: Meal Inconsistency
findings.clinicalExplanation: Highly irregular meal timing disrupting circadian rhythm and appetite hormones.
findings.userExplanation: Your irregular meal times can confuse your body's hunger signals, making it harder to recognize when you're actually hungry or full.

findings.title: Frequent Breakfast Skipping
findings.clinicalExplanation: Regular omission of the first meal of the day, potentially leading to later overcompensation.
findings.userExplanation: Skipping breakfast often leads to overeating later in the day due to a drop in blood sugar and increased hunger.

findings.title: Frequent Snacking
findings.clinicalExplanation: High frequency of eating between meals, contributing heavily to total energy intake.
findings.userExplanation: Frequent snacking can easily push you over your daily energy needs without you realizing it.

findings.title: Continuous Grazing
findings.clinicalExplanation: Absence of structured meals, eating continuously throughout the day.
findings.userExplanation: Grazing throughout the day makes it nearly impossible to track your food intake and prevents your digestive system from resting.

findings.title: Regular Late Eating
findings.clinicalExplanation: Consuming significant calories close to bedtime, negatively impacting sleep and digestion.
findings.userExplanation: Eating late at night can disrupt your sleep quality and may lead to storing more energy as fat due to lower evening activity.

findings.title: Chronic Late Eating
findings.clinicalExplanation: Habitual late-night eating, strongly correlated with circadian disruption and weight gain.
findings.userExplanation: Consistently eating large amounts late at night disrupts your body's natural rhythm and makes weight management significantly harder.

findings.title: Frequent Eating Out
findings.clinicalExplanation: High reliance on restaurant meals, which are typically higher in calories, sodium, and fat.
findings.userExplanation: Restaurant meals are often much higher in hidden fats and calories than home-cooked food, making portion control difficult.

findings.title: High Restaurant Dependency
findings.clinicalExplanation: Primary reliance on commercial food preparation, severely limiting control over nutritional intake.
findings.userExplanation: Relying heavily on takeout or restaurants means you have little control over the hidden ingredients and calories in your food.

findings.title: High Sugar Beverages
findings.clinicalExplanation: Frequent consumption of sugar-sweetened beverages.
findings.userExplanation: Sugary drinks provide empty calories that don't make you feel full, making them one of the easiest ways to over-consume energy.

findings.title: Daily Sugar Beverages
findings.clinicalExplanation: Daily intake of liquid calories, heavily impacting insulin response and energy balance.
findings.userExplanation: Drinking sugary beverages daily spikes your blood sugar and adds significant calories without satisfying your hunger.

findings.title: Excess Liquid Calories
findings.clinicalExplanation: High proportion of daily energy intake coming from fluids (sugary drinks, alcohol, lattes).
findings.userExplanation: A large part of your energy comes from drinks. Liquid calories don't register well with your brain's fullness signals, leading to overeating.

findings.title: Large Portions
findings.clinicalExplanation: Habitually consuming portion sizes larger than physiological requirements.
findings.userExplanation: Your portion sizes are likely larger than what your body actually needs for fuel.

findings.title: Very Large Portions
findings.clinicalExplanation: Consistently consuming very large portions, indicating possible leptin resistance or stretched stomach capacity.
findings.userExplanation: Consistently eating very large portions can stretch your stomach and dull your body's natural fullness signals.

findings.title: Frequent Cravings
findings.clinicalExplanation: Experiencing regular food cravings, often linked to blood sugar fluctuations or stress.
findings.userExplanation: Frequent cravings usually indicate that your meals aren't balanced enough, or that stress is driving your desire to eat.

findings.title: Persistent Cravings
findings.clinicalExplanation: Intense, ongoing cravings indicating significant metabolic or psychological distress.
findings.userExplanation: Intense, ongoing cravings are often a sign that your body is lacking specific nutrients, or that emotional stress is very high.

findings.title: Late Night Cravings
findings.clinicalExplanation: Cravings specifically occurring in the evening, often due to daytime under-eating or fatigue.
findings.userExplanation: Evening cravings are very common when you haven't eaten enough protein or calories earlier in the day, or when you are overtired.

findings.title: Emotional Eating
findings.clinicalExplanation: Using food as a coping mechanism for emotional distress.
findings.userExplanation: You tend to use food to cope with stress or emotions. Finding non-food ways to manage feelings is a key step to long-term success.

findings.title: Chronic Emotional Eating
findings.clinicalExplanation: Deeply ingrained pattern of emotional eating, requiring behavioral intervention.
findings.userExplanation: Eating has become your primary way to handle difficult emotions. Developing new coping strategies will be crucial for your progress.

findings.title: Sleep Deprivation
findings.clinicalExplanation: Severe lack of sleep, directly increasing ghrelin and decreasing leptin.
findings.userExplanation: You are severely sleep-deprived. This spikes your hunger hormones and makes craving high-calorie foods almost impossible to resist.

findings.title: Inadequate Sleep
findings.clinicalExplanation: Consistently sleeping less than the recommended 7-9 hours.
findings.userExplanation: You aren't getting enough sleep. Even a small lack of sleep can increase your appetite and reduce your motivation to exercise.

findings.title: Borderline Sleep
findings.clinicalExplanation: Sleep duration is on the lower end of the recommended range.
findings.userExplanation: Your sleep is borderline. Improving it slightly could give you a noticeable boost in energy and willpower.

findings.title: Suboptimal Sleep
findings.clinicalExplanation: Sleep duration is adequate but quality or consistency is poor.
findings.userExplanation: While you might be in bed long enough, the quality of your sleep isn't fully recharging your body.

findings.title: Poor Sleep Quality
findings.clinicalExplanation: Frequent awakenings or unrefreshing sleep despite adequate duration.
findings.userExplanation: You often wake up feeling unrefreshed, which can leave you searching for quick energy from sugary foods during the day.

findings.title: Severe Sleep Disruption
findings.clinicalExplanation: Severe disruption of sleep quality or duration, profoundly affecting metabolic regulation.
findings.userExplanation: Your sleep is severely disrupted. This makes managing your weight extremely difficult because it directly spikes hunger hormones.

findings.title: Moderate Sedentary Time
findings.clinicalExplanation: Moderate amounts of sedentary behavior throughout the day.
findings.userExplanation: You spend a moderate amount of your day sitting. Adding small, frequent movement breaks can improve your metabolic health.

findings.title: High Sedentary Behaviour
findings.clinicalExplanation: High sedentary behavior, indicating a need for structured non-exercise activity thermogenesis (NEAT).
findings.userExplanation: You spend a large part of your day sitting. Increasing your daily movement will be one of the highest leverage things you can do for your health.

findings.title: Very High Sedentary Behaviour
findings.clinicalExplanation: Prolonged and continuous sedentary behavior, a major independent risk factor for metabolic syndrome.
findings.userExplanation: You are sitting for most of your day. This signals your body to lower your metabolism, making weight loss very difficult without intervention.

findings.title: Very Low Daily Movement
findings.clinicalExplanation: Critically low incidental movement (NEAT), requiring immediate behavioral changes.
findings.userExplanation: Your incidental daily movement is very low. Even adding a 15-minute daily walk can drastically change your metabolic profile over time.

findings.title: Low Daily Movement
findings.clinicalExplanation: Overall daily step count and general movement are very low.
findings.userExplanation: Your overall daily movement is low. Simply adding a short daily walk can significantly boost your metabolism.

findings.title: Moderate Daily Movement
findings.clinicalExplanation: Acceptable but suboptimal incidental movement throughout the day.
findings.userExplanation: Your daily movement is okay, but optimizing it could give you a much larger buffer against excess calories.

findings.title: No Structured Exercise
findings.clinicalExplanation: Absence of planned, intentional physical activity.
findings.userExplanation: You currently don't have a structured exercise routine. Adding one will help build muscle and improve your metabolic health.

findings.title: Limited Exercise
findings.clinicalExplanation: Insufficient structured physical activity according to minimum clinical guidelines.
findings.userExplanation: You are getting very limited structured exercise. Resistance training or cardio is vital for maintaining muscle mass while losing weight.

findings.title: Moderate Stress
findings.clinicalExplanation: Reported moderate stress levels, potentially influencing behavioral choices.
findings.userExplanation: You're experiencing moderate stress, which can occasionally trigger emotional eating or reduce your motivation to exercise.

findings.title: High Stress
findings.clinicalExplanation: High reported stress levels, likely causing hypercortisolemia and insulin resistance.
findings.userExplanation: Your stress levels are very high. When stressed, your body holds onto energy, especially around the midsection, making fat loss very stubborn.

findings.title: Chronic Stress
findings.clinicalExplanation: Prolonged high stress, strongly associated with central adiposity and insulin resistance.
findings.userExplanation: Chronic stress can change how your body processes food, making weight loss very difficult until the stress is managed.

findings.title: Low Daily Energy
findings.clinicalExplanation: Consistently low energy levels, possibly due to poor nutrition, sleep, or metabolic inflexibility.
findings.userExplanation: You are experiencing consistently low energy. This often happens when your body isn't getting the right fuel at the right times, or from poor sleep.

findings.title: Reduced Energy
findings.clinicalExplanation: Reported drop in energy, potentially indicating an overly restrictive diet or recovery deficit.
findings.userExplanation: Your energy levels are somewhat reduced. Small tweaks to your nutrition timing or sleep quality could help you bounce back.

findings.title: Low Self Confidence
findings.clinicalExplanation: Low self-efficacy regarding weight management, increasing risk of attrition.
findings.userExplanation: You have low confidence right now, which is completely normal. We will build your belief by focusing on extremely easy, guaranteed wins.

findings.title: Moderate Self Confidence
findings.clinicalExplanation: Moderate self-efficacy, requiring supportive coaching to solidify habits.
findings.userExplanation: You are somewhat confident in your ability to succeed. Focusing on consistency rather than perfection will help you build even more momentum.

findings.title: Limited Support
findings.clinicalExplanation: Sparse social support network for behavioral changes.
findings.userExplanation: You have limited support right now. Creating an environment that makes healthy choices easier will be crucial for your success.

findings.title: No Support System
findings.clinicalExplanation: Complete lack of social support, placing full behavioral burden on the individual.
findings.userExplanation: You currently don't have a support system. This makes change harder, so we will focus on building self-reliance and finding community.

findings.title: Positive Energy Balance Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Pattern analysis indicates caloric intake consistently exceeds expenditure.
findings.userExplanation: Your overall pattern of habits suggests you are regularly taking in more energy than your body requires, which drives weight gain.

findings.title: Irregular Eating Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Pattern analysis indicates highly erratic meal timing.
findings.userExplanation: Your overall eating pattern is highly irregular, which can confuse your body's natural hunger signals and metabolic rhythm.

findings.title: Sedentary Lifestyle Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Pattern analysis indicates a profound lack of physical activity.
findings.userExplanation: Your overall lifestyle is highly sedentary. Addressing this will be one of the most impactful changes you can make for your health.

findings.title: Recovery Deficit Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Pattern analysis indicates chronic lack of restorative sleep and stress management.
findings.userExplanation: Your overall pattern shows a significant lack of recovery, which directly sabotages your body's ability to manage appetite and burn fat.

findings.title: Emotional Eating Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Pattern analysis strongly associates stress or emotion with food intake.
findings.userExplanation: Your overall pattern indicates you frequently use food to cope with emotions or stress. Learning non-food coping mechanisms is essential.

findings.title: Weight Cycling Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Pattern analysis indicates a chronic history of weight fluctuation.
findings.userExplanation: Your overall pattern shows a history of weight cycling. This means we must avoid restrictive diets and focus purely on sustainable habits.

findings.title: Unrealistic Target
findings.clinicalExplanation: Target weight is below physiological healthy limits.
findings.userExplanation: Your target weight may be lower than what is physiologically healthy or sustainable for your body.

findings.title: Unrealistic Expectation
findings.clinicalExplanation: Timeline for weight loss is overly aggressive.
findings.userExplanation: Your timeline for results is very aggressive. A slower pace will help ensure the weight stays off permanently.

findings.title: Low Behaviour Readiness
findings.clinicalExplanation: Low readiness to change, indicating need for motivational interviewing techniques.
findings.userExplanation: You aren't quite ready for major lifestyle changes yet. We will focus on tiny, almost effortless tweaks to get you started.

findings.title: Active Healthy Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Pattern analysis indicates excellent metabolic and cardiovascular activity levels.
findings.userExplanation: Your overall pattern shows you maintain an active, healthy lifestyle. This is a massive strength!

findings.title: Strong Recovery Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Pattern analysis indicates optimal sleep and stress regulation.
findings.userExplanation: Your overall pattern shows you prioritize sleep and recovery. This gives you a massive advantage in managing your health.

findings.title: Balanced Nutrition Pattern
findings.clinicalExplanation: Pattern analysis indicates strong adherence to nutritional guidelines.
findings.userExplanation: Your overall eating pattern is very balanced, providing a solid foundation for any specific health goals.
